anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves nothing: it keeps the three original-head proofs plus the origin/retry ancestor check, the missing-only ref creation, the home-only non-force push after evidence/strip/seal, the fresh post-push body fetch into an outside-repo scratch with the exact `gh pr edit 12 --repo acme/widget --body-file "$SCRATCH"` before eligibility, the full-SHA/ref Before line with capitalized combined fields and whole-PR telemetry, attributed #12/#13/#14 thread lists with the home fix proven by fffffff and member dispositions marked as member history, the verbatim close question with both URL-bearing comments, immediate rechecks before closing without `--delete-branch`, and every success/decline/stale/closed/failed-close/row-5 outcome with ship completion timing. Two small wording risks worth tightening in After: the parenthetical "(local, so no fetch is needed)" in Member eligibility could be read as skipping the live state/head refresh even though `gh pr view` is still shown, so say "no git fetch is needed; state/head come from the gh call"; and, like Before, After never states that a failed member refresh is treated as a skip, so adding one clause ("a failed or changed recheck skips that target") next to the immediate-recheck sentence would make the question fact fully explicit while still delivering the Change.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every conjunct Before kept and additionally satisfies the row-5 clause of outcomes by explicitly naming "Member PRs #13, #14 left open" where Before only said "members untouched"; it also makes ship-completion timing explicit per variant (close/skip/fail first, then complete ship, then `gauntlet: done pushed`). Two things in After are weaker than Before without breaking a fact and are worth restoring: Before explicitly tied HOME's fixed-in disposition to the captured "naming commit fffffff" (first-parent proof), whereas After only says "capture accepted-complete HOME task evidence" — write "accepted-complete HOME task with first-parent naming commit fffffff" so the attribution proof is unambiguous; and After describes the seal in prose rather than printing the `node "$BIN/gauntlet-telemetry-seal.mjs" --worktree "$WORKTREE" --option pr --base origin/main --spec "$SPEC"` call, so keep the literal command alongside the push/fetch/edit calls. Neither output states that a failed member refresh after approval is skipped (both only cover a changed head); adding "skip any target whose refresh fails or whose state/head differs" to the Answer-1 row would close that gap while leaving all other facts intact.
